speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you are presenting with chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have there been any associated changes in your bowel habits, such as blood or mucus in the stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D). The clinical presentation of chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain relieved by defecation, mucus in stool, and the sensation of incomplete evacuation in a young female is highly characteristic of IBS, and the camping history suggests a viral trigger rather than an active infectious etiology like Campylobacter.
